title: Chemical Release
description: Use this list to prepare for a hazmat or chemical release near home, and to act fast on an evacuate or shelter-in-place order.

sources.title: What to Do to Shelter in Place for a Chemical Emergency

items.text: Sign up for local emergency alerts and keep a battery radio - officials will say whether to evacuate or shelter in place
Follow the official order exactly; if told to evacuate, leave right away by the route given
If caught outside, move away from the cloud or smell, crosswind or upwind, and get inside the nearest building
Never drive into or through a visible cloud or strong chemical smell
If told to shelter: bring everyone and pets in, close and lock doors and windows
Shut off furnace, air conditioning, and all fans including bath, kitchen, and dryer; close fireplace dampers
Go to an interior room as high in the building as possible - many toxic gases sink, so avoid basements
Seal the room: plastic sheeting over windows and vents, tape all edges, wet towel under the door
Keep pre-cut 4 mil plastic sheeting, duct tape, and scissors in your chosen room
Keep water, phone and charger, medicines, and your go-kit in or near the room
In a car: close windows and vents and turn off the fan and air conditioning
If a chemical got on you: remove clothing (cut it off rather than pulling over your head), bag it, and wash skin with plenty of soap and water
Flush eyes with clean water for 10-15 minutes, removing contact lenses first
Save Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) and call 911 for breathing trouble, burns, or eye pain
Stay sheltered until officials give the all-clear - expect a few hours, not days
Afterward, open windows and doors, restart HVAC, and follow cleanup instructions for surfaces, produce, and pets
Do not go out to pick up children - schools have their own shelter plans
Learn what nearby rail lines, highways, and plants could release, and your community's alert method
